messages.subject: Coloring clades
messages.body_plain:
Hello -

Many apologies for what is likely a simple explanation. I feel a little silly because I have been going through all the vignettes and help websites, and I cannot figure out one small piece of the command to color in specific clades. Many people are using:

ggtree(treeName, aes(color = group))

but I am lost as to what the "group" refers to. I have tried the following:

nex <- system.file("bs_4_85_coal_500.tre", package="ggtree")
tree <- read.nexus("bs_4_85_coal_500.tre")
tree
tree$tip.label
tree$node.label
roottree <- root.phylo(tree, "Dlighti_7", resolve.root=TRUE)
p <- ggtree(roottree, branch.length="none", layout="fan") +
  geom_tiplab(geom = "label", offset = 1, size=2.5, fill="lightblue", hjust = .5, align = TRUE) +
  geom_nodelab(geom="label", aes(label=round(as.numeric(label, digits=0)),
  subset=!is.na <http://is.na>(as.numeric(label)) & label>50 & label != "Root" ), size=3, color = "black", hjust = -.1, fill = "lightsteelblue2")

###Assigning individuals to a clade
M_farc <- MRCA(tree, tip=c("Alaska_28", "Alaska_16", "Alaska_13", "Alaska_24", "PacificNW_15", "Japan_32", "Japan_121", "Japan_34", "PacificNW_21", "WA_PtDefiance2", "WA_PtDefiance1", "CA_MHH5B", "Alaska_8", "Alaska_4", "PacificNW_2", "PacificNW_1", "Alaska_27", "Alaska_19", "PacificNW_3"))

NA_Europe <- MRCA(tree, tip=c("Norway_27", "Norway_58", "Norway_88", "Ireland_111", "Ireland_46", "Norway_4", "Norway_117", "Norway_97"))

NA_North_America <- MRCA(tree, tip=c("NH2", "NH4", "ME_DMC33", "ME_DAR3"))

SmPac <- MRCA(tree, tip=c("CA_SLOAB1A", "CA_Pipo3A", "CA_SLOAB1C", "WA_DesMoines1", "WA_DesMoines2", "CA_Woodley4", "CA_BODD5C", "CA_SeDr1B", "CA_SeDr1E"))

clade <- c(Large=M_farc, North_Atlantic_Europe=NA_Europe, North_Atlantic_North_America=NA_North_America, Small_Pacific=SmPac)

grouptree <- groupClade(tree, clade)
roottree <- root.phylo(grouptree, "Dlighti_7", resolve.root=TRUE)
cols <- c(Large = "blue", North_Atlantic_Europe="#CA6629", North_Atlantic_North_America="#894418", Small_Pacific="#9ACD32")

ggtree(roottree, aes(color = group), ladderize = FALSE)) + geom_tiplab(aes(label = paste0("italic('", label, "')")), parse = TRUE, size = 2.5) + geom_treescale(x = 0, y = 1, width = 0.002) + scale_color_manual(values = c(cols, "black"), na.value = "black", name = "Lineage", breaks = c("Large", "North_Atlantic_Europe", "North_Atlantic_North_America", "Small_Pacific")) + guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 5, shape = 15)))

Thank you in advance for any explanation or suggestions

messages.body_plain:
For multiPhylo, you cannot use %<+% directly.
However, associating data to a set of trees is possible with the tidytree package.

Try the following code:

x <- ape::rmtree(3, 5)
d = data.frame(label = paste0('t', 1:5),
    type = sample(letters[1:3], 5, replace=T))

require(tidytree)

trees <- lapply(x, function(y) {
 full_join(as_tibble(y), d, by='label') %>% as.treedata
})

class(trees) <- 'multiPhylo'

require(ggtree)
require(ggplot2)

ggtree(trees) +
  facet_wrap(~.id) +
  geom_tippoint(aes(color=type), size = 3)

Bests,
Guangchuang
